title: Air Fryer Chicken Tenders & Fries
subtitle: panko-crusted chicken strips air-fried crisp with oven fries and a honey-lemon dip
imageAlt: Golden panko chicken tenders and fries on a white plate with a small bowl of creamy dip, on a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Cook the tenders in one layer with space between; 2 batches in most basket air fryers.
The fries go in the oven at the same time, so everything is ready together.

steps.title: Fries in the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Spread the fries in one layer on a baking sheet and bake 20–25 minutes, turning once, until crisp.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Season the chicken strips with the salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika. Put the flour, eggs and panko in 3 shallow bowls.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Dip each strip in flour, then egg, then panko, pressing so the crumbs stick. Set on a plate and brush or drizzle lightly with the oil.

steps.title: Air-fry
steps.text: Heat the air fryer to 200°C (400°F). Cook the tenders in one layer, in 2 batches, 10–12 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and 74°C (165°F) inside. Set the first batch on a rack, then return it to the basket for the last 2 minutes of the second batch to re-warm.

steps.title: Dip
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, honey and lemon juice together.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the tenders and fries on plates with the dip on the side.

fixIt.fix: They need a little oil. Brush or spray any dry spots before cooking and halfway through.
Pat the chicken dry before flouring, and press the panko on firmly.
The strips were too thin or cooked too long. Keep them about 2 cm thick and check at 9 minutes.
Spread them out in one layer and give them 5 minutes more.

saleTip: Frozen fries are often 2 for $6 at No Frills; panko lasts months in the pantry.
swap: No air fryer: bake the coated tenders on a rack set on a baking sheet at 220°C (425°F) 15–18 minutes, turning once, to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Re-crisp in the air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 4–5 minutes, then slice into a wrap with lettuce and the dip.
doneness: 74°C (165°F) in the thickest strip (Health Canada, poultry pieces); coating deep golden.
source: Based on tested air fryer chicken tender methods (Canadian Living, Instant Brands): a flour, egg and panko coating, air-fried at 200°C (400°F) for 10–12 minutes.
prepAhead: Coat the tenders up to 4 hours ahead and keep them uncovered on a rack in the fridge.
reheat: Air fryer at 190°C (375°F) 4–5 minutes, until 74°C (165°F) and crisp. Not the microwave; it makes them soggy.

basic.note: Salt, pepper and garlic powder in the coating, and ketchup instead of the dip.

stepNotes.4: Basic: skip the dip; serve with ketchup.

fancy.note: Parmesan in the crust and a little garlic in the dip.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: stir the Parmesan into the panko.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: stir the grated garlic into the dip.

plating: Fries in a paper-lined basket or bowl.
Dip in a small bowl on the plate.

why.0-5: Flour gives the egg something to grip, so the coating stays on.
why.0-7: Panko's large, airy flakes get much crunchier than regular breadcrumbs.

funFact: An air fryer is really a small, powerful convection oven: the fan moves hot air fast enough to crisp food with a spoon of oil.

keeps.note: freeze cooked tenders on a tray, then bag; reheat from frozen in the air fryer 8–10 minutes
